title: CHAPTER NINETEEN. On Gods blessedness; definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): many doubt, reasoning about His blessedness out from our satiated appetites — but in what thing His blessedness consists. in ye whole circle belonging toward ye earth, call God most blessed — all who confess that same God is. plus it stands as ye act belonging toward Gods life by means belonging toward that same which He so enjoys His infinite perfection fully known through ye intellect plus supremely loved through His will that same He wholly rests in it — there follows that same that which stands as blessedness. that same which stands as virtue: — thus far was ye integrity belonging toward Gods life. On Gods blessedness. CHAPTER NINETEEN.
pass_b_english: Thus far was the integrity of Gods life, which stands as virtue: there follows that which stands as blessedness, and it is the act of Gods life by which He so enjoys His infinite perfection fully known through the intellect and supremely loved through His will that He wholly rests in it.

All who confess that God is, in the whole circle of the earth, call God most blessed. But in what thing His blessedness consists, many doubt, reasoning about His blessedness from our satiated appetites.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM NONUM, De Dei beatitudine. Hactenus fuit integritas vitae Dei, quae se habet ut virtus: sequitur ea, quae est ut beatitas, et est actus vitae Dei, quo ille perfectione sua infinita per intellectum plene cognita et per voluntatem suam summe amata ita fruitur, ut in ea totus acquiescat. Omnes Deum dicimus beatissimum, quicunque Deum esse confitemur in toto terrarum orbe. Verum enimvero qua in re beatitudo illius consistat, dubitant multi e nostris appetitibus satiati de illius beatitate ratiocinantes.
